request.name: Brad Pitt
request.title: Actor
request.about:
William Bradley Pitt (born December 18, 1963) is an American actor and film producer. He is the recipient of various accolades, including two Academy Awards, two British Academy Film Awards, two Golden Globe Awards, and a Primetime Emmy Award. One of the most influential celebrities, Pitt appeared on Forbes' annual Celebrity 100 list from 2006 to 2008, and the Time 100 list in 2007. His films as a leading actor have grossed over $6.9 billion worldwide.

Pitt first gained recognition as a cowboy hitchhiker in the Ridley Scott road film Thelma & Louise (1991). Pitt emerged as a star taking on leading man roles in films such as the drama A River Runs Through It (1992), the western Legends of the Fall (1994), the horror film Interview with the Vampire (1994), the crime thriller Seven (1995), and the cult film Fight Club (1999). Pitt found greater commercial success starring in Steven Soderbergh's heist film Ocean's Eleven (2001), and reprised his role in its sequels. He cemented his leading man status starring in blockbusters such as the historical epic Troy (2004), the romantic crime film Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005), the horror film World War Z (2013), and the action film Bullet Train (2022).

Pitt won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for playing a stuntman in Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019). He was Oscar-nominated for his roles in the science fiction drama 12 Monkeys (1995), the fantasy romance The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (2008) and the sports drama Moneyball (2011). He also starred in acclaimed films such as Babel (2006), The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford (2007), Burn After Reading (2008), Inglourious Basterds (2009), The Tree of Life (2011), and The Big Short (2015).

In 2001, Pitt co-founded the production company Plan B Entertainment. As a producer he won the Academy Award for Best Picture for 12 Years a Slave (2013) and was nominated for Moneyball (2011) and The Big Short (2015). Pitt was named People's Sexiest Man Alive in 1995 and 2000.

events.event: His 18-year-old daughter, Vivienne, filed a petition in the Los Angeles County Superior Court to legally drop 'Pitt' from her surname, following similar steps taken by her siblings amid ongoing fallout from the high-profile family separation.
Starred as veteran racing driver Sonny Hayes in the high-budget Formula 1 racing drama film 'F1', directed by Joseph Kosinski.
His protracted, multi-year divorce and legal disputes involving ex-wife Angelina Jolie reached a formal conclusion.
Co-starred alongside George Clooney in the action-comedy thriller film 'Wolfs', which received a streaming release on Apple TV+.
Attended the world premiere of his co-produced biographical sports drama film 'The Boys in the Boat', directed by George Clooney.
Starred as silent-film era icon Jack Conrad in Damien Chazelle's ambitious Hollywood historical drama 'Babylon'.
Starred as assassin Ladybug in the fast-paced action-comedy film 'Bullet Train', directed by David Leitch.
Won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor at the 92nd Academy Awards for his performance as stuntman Cliff Booth in Quentin Tarantino's 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood'.
Starred as astronaut Roy McBride in James Gray's existential sci-fi drama film 'Ad Astra'.
Played the iconic role of Cliff Booth alongside Leonardo DiCaprio in Quentin Tarantino's critically acclaimed 9th film, 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood'.
Angelina Jolie filed for divorce from Brad Pitt after two years of marriage and over a decade together, triggering extensive international media coverage.
Won his first Academy Award as a producer when 'The Big Short' (which he co-produced and co-starred in) won the Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay.
Married his long-time partner and actress Angelina Jolie in a private ceremony at Château Miraval in Correns, France.
Starred as United Nations employee Gerry Lane in the high-grossing apocalyptic zombie thriller film 'World War Z'.
Starred as Oakland Athletics general manager Billy Beane in the sabermetric baseball drama 'Moneyball', earning Academy Award nominations for both Best Actor and Best Picture (as producer).
Starred as Lt. Aldo Raine in Quentin Tarantino's World War II alternate-history masterwork 'Inglourious Basterds'.
Starred in David Fincher's fantasy drama 'The Curious Case of Benjamin Button', receiving his second Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.

Founded the prominent American production company Plan B Entertainment alongside Jennifer Aniston and Brad Grey (later taking sole control in 2005), which went on to produce multiple Best Picture Oscar-winning films.
Married actress Jennifer Aniston in a private, high-profile wedding ceremony in Malibu, California.
Starred as the enigmatic Tyler Durden alongside Edward Norton in David Fincher's cult classic psychological masterpiece 'Fight Club'.
Starred alongside Morgan Freeman as Detective David Mills in David Fincher's landmark neo-noir psychological thriller 'Se7en'.
Had his major breakout Hollywood role as the charming hitchhiker J.D. in Ridley Scott's critically acclaimed road-crime film 'Thelma & Louise'.
Born as William Bradley Pitt to William Alvin Pitt and Jane Etta Hillhouse in Shawnee, Oklahoma, United States.
